units.la: O Respublica quàm beata: cujus Clavum vir tenet eruditus atque Prudens! Imperio sub hujus artes Florent & pietas: atrox Erinnys Exulat: rabidus siletque Mavors: Servantur veneranda jura: vera Quae sunt ingenuè eloquuntur omnes. Consultissime Vir, celebriori Nate stemmate BREDERODIORUM, Ordinum Imperium potentiorum; Quos concordia junxit, est beatum Ipso hoc nomine: splendidissima hujus Gubernacula quòd tenent probati, Prudentes viri & eruditi. Eorum Quippe fidâ ope gloriam paravit Isthanc; undique quae refulget orbe: Qua tot belligeros, solo salo, hostes Fudit, contudit, & subegit, armis juste pro Patria Fidéque sumtis: Triumfis tot ovavit inclytis: tot Onustum spoliis, Americanis, Indicis, Orientis, Occidentis, Longas, difficiles, periculosas Victrices per expeditiones; Suos sæpe redivit ad penates. O beatum igitur: quater beatum. Sed horum in grege fulgido virorum,
units.tr: O happy Commonwealth, whose helm a learned and prudent man holds! Under his rule the arts flourish, and piety too, while cruel Erinys is banished and raging Mars is silent. Venerable laws are kept, and all men speak what is true, frankly. Most wise sir, distinguished by the famous stock of the Brederodes, you lead the Empire of the mightier States, which concord has joined together; the state is blessed by this very name, because upright, prudent and learned men hold its most splendid helm. By their faithful aid this State has won a glory that shines throughout the world: by arms justly taken up for country and faith, it has routed, crushed and subdued so many warlike enemies on land and sea, and has celebrated so many famous triumphs. Laden with spoils from America, India, the East and the West, it has returned home to its household gods after long, difficult and dangerous victorious expeditions. O happy, therefore; four times happy. But in the shining band of these men,

units.la: Quòd juvas quoque tu, domi foràsque,
units.tr: That you also help, at home and abroad,
Your father's rule, with honest, faithful,
Firm, manly strength,
Of lofty counsel, experience and skill,
And of prudence and eloquence, the gifts

units.la: Quæ Dei munera sunt: vocaris o quàm
units.tr: Of gracious God; how rightly you are called,
By every right, to me, by anagram,
PRUDENT STRENGTH and the Ordained of God!
Of my hundred thousand patrons,
Best of patrons! Of the BREDERODES
The ample, conspicuous and golden star!
Francis Castillionaeus:
I stand, an unharmed and gentle infant.
O Christ, eternal offspring of the almighty Father, redeemer of the universe,
who by your word promised the little child
I acknowledge my filth, defiled and humble, and I curse it with a wailing that sounds like grief.
that he would be heir of blessed joy:
and oil; he places him on his little donkey;
Behold, I stand before you as an infant stands before its parent, gentle and tame.

units.la: En en mihi tibi si STO, sicut INFANS
units.tr: I acknowledge my humble stain, polluted and cursed by my tearful lament.
Wipe it out, wash it away, and anoint it: all the iniquity you cast away from here,
as far as the earth is distant from the pole of heaven,
as far as the west is distant from the east.
Blot this out, wash it away, and smear over the whole of it.
You who cast away such wickedness from here,

units.la: Quantum distat ab axe terra Olympi,
units.tr: As far as the earth lies from the axis of Olympus,

units.la: Quantum dissitus occidens ab ortu est.
units.tr: As far as the west is distant from the east.
You are yourself easily entreated, yourself gentle,
Slow to stir up dark bile.

units.la: ILLÆSVM sed &, ō Deus benigne, Sisto me tibi, non quidem innocenti Natura merito mea; luem qui Vel mecum ex utero parentis hausi; Nempe infectus originis veneno: Verùm justitiæ tuæ, Redemtor, Indutus chlamyde innocentiaque. Hanc cùm mente fideique filiali; Quæ fructus tamen interim haud sit expers, Instar arboris efficacioris, Et credam, mihi & applicem, puellus Illæsus tuus & queam vocari, Hyssopo crucis & tuæ piari. Pro virtutibus his; quibus coronas Me; quibus reficis measque vires, Vt undis aquila innovat juventam, Sint, sint, sint tibi gratiæ perennes Nostri o Conditor optime! o Redemtor Vne! o Sanctificator uber. Amen.
units.tr: Unharmed yet also, O gracious God, I present myself to you. I am not innocent by any merit of my nature, since I drew the plague with me from my parent's womb, infected indeed with the poison of origin. But, Redeemer, I am clothed in your righteousness and innocence. I hold this with a mind and a filial faith, which is nevertheless not without fruit in the meantime, like a more effective tree. And let me believe it and apply it to myself, so that I may be called your unharmed little child, cleansed with the hyssop of the cross and of yours. For these virtues, with which you crown me, with which you restore me and my strength, as the eagle renews its youth in the waters, may there be, may there be, may there be everlasting thanks to you, O best Creator of ours! O sole Redeemer! O bountiful Sanctifier. Amen.

units.la: IOANNES CAROLUS A BOTZHEIM: Heic zelo bono Samaritanus.
units.tr: JOHN CHARLES OF BOTZHEIM: Here, a Samaritan with good zeal.

units.la: VRbem palmiferam petens Hebræus Latronum spoliatur a caterva; Diro vulnere quæ relinquit illum Læsum, seminecem. Piger sacerdos Illac præterit & Levita: rident, Negligunt hominem, haut eum allocuti. Zelo Samaritanus ardet: ægrum Adit: sublevat: ulcera atra mundat,
units.tr: Making for the palm-bearing city, a Hebrew is stripped by a band of robbers. They leave him wounded by a dreadful blow, injured and half-dead. A lazy priest passes that way, and a Levite: they laugh, they neglect the man, and they do not so much as speak to him. The Samaritan burns with zeal: he approaches the sick man, lifts him up, and cleanses his black ulcers,
binds them, pouring on a soft wine
and oil; he sets him on a little donkey;
he accompanies him to an inn.

units.la: En en denarii tibi duo, inquit,
units.tr: Behold, he says, here are two little coins for you, host,
age the man in need;
refresh him with food, wine, and a bed,
so that a skilled surgeon may
care for him. When I return, I will repay
whatever you have spent. Aptly and elegantly,
Carolus, unblemished, here you seem to me
that Samaritan of good ZEAL.
When I recall each of your gifts of mind,
best and greatest, and yet above all
those known to me and to others,
I see the burning Christian piety in you.
For the grievous wounds and harmful blows
of wickedness and a sinful life, which Satan, that vast robber,

units.la: Vitæ; quas Satan, ille latro vastus,
units.tr: inflicted through the poison of origin,
many others pass by, laugh at, or approve in their own kinsmen;
but you, like another Samaritan, eagerly
strive to bring a remedy to them, stirred by the best zeal,
with the healing oil of rebuke, with the fragrant odour of admonitions,
and with the sound wine of wise counsel, while turning over in your heart
the pious words of Solomon. The fumes of frankincense
soothe hearts; but rebuking or admonishing
With the pure wine of sound counsel, you were eager to offer
the pious words of Solomon,
turning them over in your heart, the Thurian vapours
soothe the hearts; but when you rebuke or warn

units.la: Fidè, non minùs est suâvis illis:
units.tr: faithfully, they are no less sweet to them.

units.la: Quem quis diligit, hunc monet: monendo Hunc & vulnerat: at periculosa Ejus basia sunt: atroce qui te Infestans odio deosculatur.
units.tr: Whoever loves a person warns him, and in warning also wounds him; but dangerous are the kisses of one who, attacking you with savage hatred, kisses you.

units.la: VVALTHERVS RETICHIVS: Tu vir charus Helvetiis.
units.tr: VALTHERUS RETICHIUS: You, a man dear to the Helvetians.

units.la: PRaeclarißime Vir, Retichiorum Gentis gloria, Principisque dulce Tui delicium: quod a Latinis Trito fertur adagio Poëtis, Fatis nomina congruunt frequenter: Pulchrè juppiter id tibi applicarim. Nam quòd HELVETIIS suâvis atq; CHARUS VIR sies: hic vel unus actus Clarè comprobat, auspicante jovâ, Tuo Principe sic jubente, fedus Tam laudabile, forte, Christianum Quod tu dexteritate singulari, Fide, judicio, eloquentiaque, Felix sollicitâris, impetrâris, Fedus Principe Marchione dignum: Binâ & principe Civitate dignum: jure hinc surgit honor tibi perennis: jure hinc surgit amor tibi perennis. Macte hoc, macte animo! juvare Christi Gloriam, patriæ bonumque perge. Vides Imperium ut labascit: ejus Robur ut quatitur rebellione:
units.tr: Most distinguished sir, glory of the Rhaetian people and sweet darling of your Prince! As the Latin poets' common saying goes, names often agree with fates, and Jupiter, I could well apply that to you. For that you are sweet to the Helvetians and a dear man is clearly shown by this one act: under the auspices of Jove, with your Prince ordering it, you have by your singular skill, faith, judgement and eloquence happily managed to obtain so praiseworthy a covenant, a Christian one, worthy of a Prince-Marquis and of a city with its twofold rule. From this honour will rise to you forever; from this love will rise to you forever. Well done, well done in spirit! Go on helping the glory of Christ and the good of your country. You see how the Empire totters, how its strength is shaken by rebellion,

units.la: Sancta ut jura cadunt ruuntque: Vt toto furit Antichristus orbe, Et sophismatis, & dolis, & armis, Tot satellitibus, potentibúsque. Hic hic ergo animísque viribúsque Conjunctis opus est: valere Christi Si laudem & patriæ statum velimus.
units.tr: how holy laws fall and collapse, how Antichrist rages across the whole world, with his sophistries, tricks and arms, with so many henchmen and powerful men. Here, then, with minds and strength joined together, there is need of work, if we wish to be worthy of Christ's praise and of our country's condition.
GEORGIUS REMUS: Outstanding on the wall.

units.la: VRbs famosa periculosiori Hostis obsidione cùm laborat, Cives munera perprobè exsequuntur: In templo pia vota libat unus: In muro excubat alter: hic cruentum Acer ferrum acuit: sedet senatu Divorum in medio ille, quo minacem Hostem mænibus arceant. Togati est Ordinis typus iste: quo videmus In cœtu populi bene instituto, Intra limina porticúsque templi, Intra & compita, & urbis angiportus, Pulchrè munera ut exsequantur omnes. Sed magis tamen ardui Quirites, Quàm, quaeso, patria excubant? rebelles Quàm franant, reprimunt? licentiosè Peccantes domitant, bonósque servant? In horum genere arduo, diserte REME, millibus è meis amicis Antistes mihi, cùm nihil relinquas Intentatum adeò, inclyta ac potentiù NORICAE ut vigiles probè salu ti Fido consilio, eruditione Insigni, experientiâ absolutâ, Legum cognitione singulari: Ecquis non queat approbare, Miles Quod MVRO EGREGIVS sIES probusq; Tuas egregiè tuendo partes, Tuámque egregiè colendo spartam.
units.tr: When a famous city labours under a more dangerous siege by an enemy, the citizens carry out their duties most faithfully. In the temple one offers up pious prayers; another keeps watch on the wall; this one sharpens the bloody steel, and that one sits in the midst of the Senate of the gods, so that they may keep the threatening enemy away from the walls. That is the picture of the gown-wearing order, in which we see, in a well-ordered assembly of the people, within the thresholds and porticoes of the temple, and within the crossroads and narrow lanes of the city, all men carrying out their duties well. But, citizens, who keep watch for the fatherland more keenly, I ask, than these? Who curbs and restrains the rebels? Who subdues the wrongdoers who sin without restraint, and keeps the good safe? In this difficult business, Remus, outstanding in eloquence, out of my many friends you are my adviser, since you leave nothing untried, so that you keep watch well for the safety of the most famous and powerful city of Nuremberg, with faithful counsel, outstanding learning, complete experience and a singular knowledge of the laws. Who could not approve that you are an outstanding soldier and an upright man, who defend your duties outstandingly and keep your Sparta outstandingly?
IOANNES IM THURN: I lean on the Muse.

units.la: QVantum dant alii mero bibendo: Quantum pondera congerendo gazæ: Quantum sylvicolas feras sequendo: Quantum belligerando cum profanis: Quantum mercibus arte distrahendis: Quantum difficili profectioni Vel septemgemini ad vireta Nili: Quantum mille aliis decem ac trecentis Dant exercitiisve, naniisve: Tantum temporis & laboris ipse MVSAE contribuo meæ polita, In sacris studiis & in profanis: Huic INNITOR, adhæreo, vacouni: Hanc amo, foveo, osculor, colo unam: Me vicissim amat illa: me tuetur, Solatur, monet, erudit, movetque Ad quodvis genus eruditionis, Ad quodvis genus elegantiarum.
units.tr: However much others give to drinking wine, however much to piling up the weight of treasure, to hunting the forest beasts, to fighting with the profane, to selling goods with skill, to the difficult journey to the green fields of the sevenfold Nile, however much they give to a thousand other pursuits, dances or games, so much time and labour I myself, in polished studies, both sacred and profane, give to my Muse alone. To her I lean, to her I cling, and I am free for her alone. I love her, cherish her, kiss her, and worship her alone. She in turn loves me; she protects me, comforts me, advises me, teaches me, and moves me to every kind of learning and every kind of elegance.

units.la: Nec non ad genus omne sanctitatis: Linguas, eloquium, atque disputare Me docet; numerare, cantitare, Terram & astra metirier: velipsas Me per Historias amoeniores, Deducit: loca, facta, nationes, In Europa, Asia, Affrica, Indiisque Quae sunt, queque fuere, differentes. Hic mentem recreat meam Thuanus: Illic mille alii, novi, vetusti, Quotquot Historici fuere, suntque, Vitam perpoliunt meam, viasque Docent justitia supra ambulare. Quid multa? Vber & almus ille Rhenus Non tot piscículis bonis natatur: Non tot & prope fluctibus tumescit: Non tot capreoli ruunt per alpes: Non tot undique casei premuntur Dulces, molliculi, recentiores: Non tot miles habet paternus hastas: Quot rivi utilitatis hinc redundant, Magnae, mirificae, atque inexplicandae: Et Musa duce cum mea redundent, jure hanc deligo, diligóque, amóque: Huic INNITOR, adhaereóque jure, Vni, & assidue, atque ubique: Mundi Vanitatibus omnibus relictis.
units.tr: Likewise she teaches me every kind of holiness; she teaches me languages, eloquence, and how to dispute; to count, to sing, to measure the earth and the stars; and she herself leads me through more pleasant histories: the places, deeds and nations of Europe, Asia, Africa and the Indies, both those that are and those that have been, all different. Here Thuanus refreshes my mind; there a thousand others, new and old, as many as there have been and are historians, polish my life and teach me that my ways should go beyond justice. What more? That broad and bountiful Rhine does not swim with so many good little fish, nor swell with so many waves nearly, nor do so many roe deer rush through the Alps; nowhere are so many sweet, soft, fresh cheeses pressed; my paternal soldier does not have so many spears, as many streams of usefulness flow from her, great, wonderful and inexhaustible. And since they flow with my Muse as guide, I rightly choose her, cherish her and love her. To her alone, constantly and everywhere, I rightly lean and cling, with all the vanities of the world left behind.
IACOBUS STUDER:

units.la: Tu Deo bis carus, Verba custodis, Ab corde justus.
units.tr: You, dear to God twice over, keeper of words, just from the heart.

units.la: QVᴀ David, generosus ille vates, Perquàm magnificè est locutus olim: Qui purus scelerum, integérque vitæ, Quod justum est facit, atque veritatem Cordis eruit è suì recessu: Qui non ore solet calumniari: Vicino mala nec creat: vel ullo Probro eum afficit: unius nec assis Aestimat reprobum, at colit probatum: Qui fidem temerare pactam abhorret, Vsuræ gravis hostis, & rapinæ: Nec munus super innocente quærens: Is carissimus est Deo, haud movetur, Sed vel æthereâ locatur aulâ, &c.
units.tr: What David, that noble poet, once said most magnificently: he who is pure of sin and whole in life, who does what is just and draws out truth from the recesses of his heart; who is not in the habit of slandering with his mouth, who does no evil to his neighbour and casts no reproach on him; who values no reprobate at a single penny, but honours the approved; who shrinks from breaking a pledged faith, a grave enemy of usury and plunder; who seeks no bribe against the innocent. He is most dear to God, is not moved, but is set even in the heavenly hall, and so on.

units.la: Hæc, STVDERE, ego singula applicare Possim muneribus tuis politis: Quis te dia benignitas beavit.
units.tr: I could apply each of these things, STUDER, to your polished gifts. What gracious kindness has blessed you?

units.la: Námque AB CORDE, manu, ore JVSTVS atque Purus quòd sies, & crees propinquo Nec perjuria, nec malum, fidelis Custos sed fidei audiaris: almâ Est notum in patriâ urbe. SANCTO GALLI: Est notúmque alibi, Italis, Britannis, Gallis, Teutonibúsque, Sarmatisque: Quorum tu loca, facta & instituta
units.tr: For that you are just from the heart, by hand and by mouth, and pure, and are heard to be a faithful keeper of faith, without perjury or malice, is known in your fatherland city of St. Gall, and is known elsewhere too, among Italians, Britons, Gauls, Germans and Sarmatians, whose places, deeds and institutions
you know all of, both the older

units.la: Tum recentia. Luculenteristud Probat, comprobat, arguitve, TV quod CARVS sis Domino DEO benigno, Bis, ter, et quater, ampliúsq; CARVS.
units.tr: and the recent. This most clearly proves, shows, or argues that you are dear to the gracious Lord God, twice, three times, four times, and yet more dear.

units.la: MELCHIOR GVLDIVS: Hic Sol rudi legum.
units.tr: MELCHIOR GVLDIVS: Here is the sun of the law to the unskilled.

units.la: Solmanè exoriens fugat tenebras: Orbi lumina fundit universo, Laborantibus, ambulantibusque.
units.tr: Rising in the morning, it drives away the shadows and pours its light on the whole world, on those who labour and on those who walk about.

units.la: Vtrúnque applicat annagrammatismus Tibi, clare vir, archigrammatée Terse, gloria magna GVLDIORVM.
units.tr: An anagram applies both of these to you, distinguished man, with a finely wrought pen, Terse, the great glory of the Guldins.

units.la: Nam quibus patria sua statuta, Ceu noctis tenebrae tenebricosae, Minùs cognita sunt, minúsque trita: Tu his, qua praditus es sacratiorum Legum cognitione singulari, Celso judicio, eloquentiáque, Ceu lumina Solis administras:
units.tr: For those whose native laws are less known and less familiar to them, like the shadows of a murky night, you, endowed with your singular knowledge of the most sacred laws, with your lofty judgement and eloquence, supply as the light of the sun.

units.la: Veracem egregiè explicando sensum: At sophismata detegendo, nodos Solvendo variósque tortilésque.
units.tr: By expounding the true meaning admirably, and by exposing sophisms and untying knots, however many and however twisted.

units.la: Testes sunt celebres profestiones Tuæ difficiles, laboriosæ: Testis est grave splendidúmque munus, Quo cum laudis honore SANCTOGALLI, Vrbe fungeris in tua paterna,
units.tr: Your difficult and laborious professions are witnesses of this, and so is the weighty and splendid office which you hold, with the honour of praise, in your native city of St Gall.
O most beautiful anagram, and true besides!
Chief scribe of St Gall, etc.
GVILLIELMVS ZIEGLERVS:
His royal zeal for the laws.

units.la: GErmen nobile, & arctiore vinclo Fida amicitiæ mihi ligate,
units.tr: Noble offspring, bound to me by the closer chain of faithful friendship,

units.la: ZIEGLERE, allubet hic tibi applicare, Quæ rex maximus Israelis olim, Zelo percitus æstuante, voouit:
units.tr: Ziegler, it pleases me to apply to you here what the greatest king of Israel once vowed, stirred by a burning zeal:

units.la: Iova æterne, benignitatis auctor, Si me lumine videris sereno: Cautus innocuæ studebo vitæ, Et, ut tota domus sit in tegella, Non exempla sequar scelestiorum, Sed horrebo operas scelestiorum, A me côrque nefarium exulabit: Non agnoscam ut amicum iniquiorem: Linguæ spicula qui jacit, propinqui In famam, exitio hunc putabo dignum: Qui supercilio efferatus omnes Temnit præse, hunc odio putabo dignum, Rursum lumina dirigam ad fideles; Grati mecum habitent ut inquilini: Is, qui vir probus est, demum suave Mihi servitium exhibebit: ullum Nec ferent mea tecta fraudulentum: Aut unquam bene habebit aut beate, Qui mendacia nonnisi loquetur: At quantocyus improbos repellam; Ut Iovæ semel exulent ab urbe Vnā omnes scelerum omnium ministri
units.tr: Eternal Jehovah, author of goodness, if you look upon me with a serene light, I shall be careful to live an innocent life. And so that my whole house may be a tent, I will not follow the examples of the wicked, but will abhor the works of the wicked; a perverse heart shall depart from me. I will not acknowledge a more unjust friend. Whoever hurls the darts of his tongue against his neighbour's reputation, I will count worthy of destruction. Whoever, puffed up with haughty brows, scorns everyone, I will count worthy of hatred. Again I will turn my eyes to the faithful, that they may dwell with me as grateful inmates. He who is an upright man shall at last render me sweet service. No deceitful person shall be borne in my house. Nor shall he who speaks only lies ever prosper or be happy. But as quickly as I can, I will drive out the wicked, so that all the ministers of all crimes may be banished at once from the city of Jehovah.

units.la: O votum bene! o tibi peraptum; Labe qui procul atque falsitate,Tum Deo cupis ipse perprobari:Tum cupisque alios probari: LEGVMZelo praeditus & bono, atq; magno,Verè Davidicóque, REGIOQUE.
units.tr: O vow well made! O most fitting for you: "Who, far from stain and falsehood, desire then to be approved before God himself; then desire that others too be approved." Of the laws, endowed with zeal, good and great, truly Davidic, and royal. ## FRANCISCUS DE VEIRAS:
Secure in the sacred Faith.

units.la: Sacra, salvifica est Fides; supremiQuae jovae auxilio quiescit uno;Christi quae merito quiescit uno;Fuso sanguine quod suo peregit.Hac qui praeditus est Fide; periclìTutus degit is omnis, haut movetur,Haut nutat, trepido haut metu pavescit,Etsi terra dehiscat: universusEtsi sursum eat activitatis orbis.
units.tr: Sacred and saving is Faith, the highest of all, which rests on the one help of Jehovah; which rests on the one merit of Christ, which he accomplished by shedding his own blood. He who is endowed with this Faith lives wholly safe from every danger; he is not moved, does not waver, does not tremble with fearful dread, though the earth gape open, though the whole orb of activity should rise upward.

units.la: VEIRASI optime, splendidissime, ipsaHac Fide quia niteris: jehovaVt tuum columen, tuae salutisCornu, praesidium tuum sit unus:Sit Christus tuus ut Redemtor unus;Nostra crimina qui piavit unus:Ne SECVRVS ab omnibus pericloHac IN salvifica SACRAtioreFIDE nixus agus: tuos in hostesTriumfas, Satanam, Luem inquinatam,Mundum, catera monstra, quo fateriPossis ore hilariq; liberóque:Te fiducia nititur mea uno:Tu meum auxilium optimum in periclo es:
units.tr: Most excellent and most splendid Veiras, since you lean upon this very Faith: may Jehovah be your pillar, the horn of your salvation, your one protection; may Christ be your one Redeemer, who alone expiated our sins; that you may live secure from every danger, leaning on this sacred and most saving Faith; may you triumph over your enemies, Satan, the defiling plague, the world, and the other monsters, so that you may be able to confess with a cheerful and free mouth. My trust rests on you alone; you are my best help in danger.

units.la: Tute virga mea & pedum, jehova, es:
units.tr: Thou, Jehovah, art my rod and my staff.
Why then should I be ashamed, or blush?
Why then should I tremble and quake with fear?
Why, if I walk through the deadly shadows, if I walk through the valley of the Styx, should I fear

units.la: Cur, si lethiferus eam per umbras,
units.tr: any phantoms at all, with you leading me and guarding me?
Rather, your goodness will attend me

units.la: Vllas, te duce me tuente larvas?
units.tr: on every side. As long as I survive,
I will enjoy the light; and then, when I am gone,
I will dwell with you forever in the abodes of your house.
LEONARTVS VVEISSIVS: Sight pleasantly fragrant.

units.la: Tecum in secla domi tuae morabor.
units.tr: A most beautiful experience, and the arts
which, far from home, indeed,
Frenchman, German, Spaniard, Italian, Briton,
your excellent experience and the arts
which, far from home, you have surely acquired,
among the French, Germans, Spanish, Italians, English,
and the Belgians, and others,
whose places, deeds and institutions
you have lately seen in a long course.
Grow, O flower of the most choice fragrance, grow under well-omened stars.
Patrician of Augsburg, etc.
and the Belgians have produced, and others,
whose places, deeds and customs
you have recently seen over a long course.
Grow, O flower of most excellent fragrance and scent, under well-omened stars, grow!
Patrician of Augsburg, etc.
In a long course you have recently been seen.
Grow, O you of well-omened stars,
Most choice flower and fragrance, grow.
Patrician of Augsburg, etc.

units.la: Nomen quó tibi pullulet perenne:Crescat quó tibi laus, decus perenne.
units.tr: That your name may sprout for you perpetually; that praise and honour may grow for you perpetually.
Bartholomaeus Vincentius:
The blessed swan, conquering life.

units.la: PRinceps inter aves Olor putatur:Doctrinæ est typus elegantioris:Pectoris nota candidi: DeorumQuondam delicium: eloquentiorem,Fata cùm sua prævidet, canoroFundit gutture naniam. Peraptè,Vincenti, tibi cuncta congruunt. Sed audi,Vitæ millia quòd pericla sentis,Sustines, superásq. ChristianoMore: rectè anagrammati vocárisVINCENS VITA MOLOR. units.tr: The swan is thought to be the prince of birds. It is a figure of more refined learning, a sign of a white breast, once the darling of the gods. When it foresees its own fate, it pours forth a more eloquent dirge from its tuneful throat. Vincentius, all these things fit you perfectly. For you are the foremost engraver of all the Gallic printers there have been, are, and will be. The books polished by your labour bear witness to this, in Greek, Chaldean, Latin and Hebrew, as do the other learned writings that have come to light through your work. Besides this, you shine with no small learning and an upright mind. You are the delight of the true God, since you confess his orthodox doctrines of the Word. O happy swan! O blessed gifts that make blessed those who hold them! But hear this: since you feel thousands of dangers to life, you endure them and overcome them in the Christian manner. Rightly are you named by an anagram of your name, which says "conquering life," the swan. O more blessed are those who suffer a thousand and a hundred persecutions in the name of Christ! For them, at last, there will be a rich reward in heaven.

units.la: VVOLFGANGVS VVOLLENSCHLEGERVS: Oh, fulge longus, ceu vernus Gallus.
units.tr: WOLFGANG WOLLENSCHLEGER: Oh, shine long, like a spring cock.

units.la: GAllus nuncius est amoenus alma Lucis: sidera gloriosa sentit: Quacunque excubat in domo, popello Suo pennigero imperat: triumfans, Si vincat, canit, atque principem se Testatur, rutilam erigendo cristam: Visu territat & trucem leonem. Hæc VVOLFGANGE, tibi omnia applicantur: Lucis nuncius es serenus almæ, Dum quæ filia lucis est, rotundo Profers ore subinde veritatem: Sentis sidera gloriosa, cœli Dum mysteria sempiterna sentis: In quocunque loco, domi foris-ve Sedes imperium asseris paterna Gentis, ingenio expolitiore: Vincendo canis, & canendo vincis, Quot sunt, quotque fuere Musicorum Omnes; quis merito queas levare Donis, ingenuo rubore cristas: Ob quæ ringat amarus ipse Satan, Leo maximus invidissimusque. His virtutibus, hisce gratiisque FVLGE OH LONGVS in optima, ampla secla: GALLVS vivere CEV solet creatus VERE longior: elegantiorum O virûm alter Apollo Musicorum!
units.tr: The cock is a pleasant herald of kindly light. He perceives the glorious stars. Wherever he keeps watch in the house, he commands his feathered people. Triumphing when he wins, he crows and proclaims himself their prince, raising his ruddy crest. By his sight he even terrifies the fierce lion. All this applies to you, Wolfgang. You are the serene herald of kindly light, since, as a daughter of light, you bring forth truth from your round mouth from time to time. You perceive the glorious stars while you perceive the eternal mysteries of heaven. In whatever place, at home or abroad, you assert the paternal rule of your nation with a more polished wit. Conquering, you sing; singing, you conquer. Of all the musicians who are and have been, whom could one rightly raise with gifts, and with an ingenuous blush, to the crest? On account of this, bitter Satan himself gnashes, the greatest and most envious lion. With these virtues and graces, shine, O long one, through the best and widest ages. May you live as Gallus, truly created longer than the spring cock, O other Apollo of the more elegant musicians!
THE END.
